heading: Test error can fall, rise, and fall again during training
definition: test error over training time follows the same fall-rise-fall shape.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce this pattern under specific training conditions, but the unqualified claim is contested. Sweeps of neural networks on tabular data fail to produce it, and adjusting step sizes can remove or reduce it.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: R2 for conditional temporal curves. <1B: R2 for conditional loss/error trajectories, alongside non-findings. At 1-10B, 10-100B and >100B: ? for strict V2 from the OPT evidence. Its selected-token rise-and-recovery trajectories are partial evidence, classified limits_scope; the initial decrease required by V2 is not established. Aggregate OPT perplexity declines monotonically.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to the unqualified claim: the reviewed tabular-network study reports unsuccessful sweeps designed to elicit the effect (arXiv:2207.12547#R3, arXiv:2207.12547#R4, arXiv:2207.12547#R5). Conditional reproduction remains documented for CNN and ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with 20% random label noise; adjusted step sizes eliminate the CNN shape and mitigate the ResNet-18 shape according to the body (arXiv:2007.10099#R9, arXiv:2007.10099#R10, arXiv:2007.10099#R11, arXiv:2007.10099#R12). That study's publication-review status is unverified in the supplied text. An explicitly sized diffusion-distillation extension appears in arXiv:2505.20123#r3. OPT 6.7B, 13B, 30B and 175B show rise and recovery on tokens selected for an upward trend after 10% of OPT 1.3B training; an initial decrease is not separately established, so these results are partial for strict V2 and warrant limits_scope rather than supports (arXiv:2212.09803#r15, arXiv:2212.09803#r16, arXiv:2212.09803#r17, arXiv:2212.09803#r18). Aggregate curves decline monotonically (arXiv:2212.09803#r1, arXiv:2212.09803#r2, arXiv:2212.09803#r3, arXiv:2212.09803#r4, arXiv:2212.09803#r5, arXiv:2212.09803#r6). counts: versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies=4 and versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies=48 are script counts before checker corrections; these overlapping verdict categories are not votes. Scale coverage comes from versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_size. versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size has no 10-100B or >100B entry.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched-recipe comparison resolving the noisy-image disagreements, robust replication of the tabular non-finding or recovery under specified conditions, and controlled aggregate within-run language-model curves at larger scales would change this assessment. Metric, token selection, schedule, noise and observation horizon need to be held explicit.

source.title: Deep double descent: where bigger models and more data hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

original_result.setup: In the original study, Nakkiran et al. tracked ResNet18 test error over training epochs on CIFAR-10 using Adam.
original_result.result: With 15% label noise and up to 4K epochs, sufficiently large models showed error falling, rising near interpolation, then falling again. The pattern also appeared with 20% noise and augmentation; varying-noise experiments showed that final error could fall below the first minimum.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Noisy-label CNN test accuracy dipped, then recovered beyond its early-stopping best.
Equal step sizes and initialization scales yielded fall-rise-fall test error across tested settings.
ResNet-18 reproduced epoch-wise double descent under ERM with noisy labels.
Noisy-label ResNet and VGG models showed a second test-error descent after memorization.
Gradient-descent bias was nonmonotonic over time in anisotropic linear regression.
Validation loss rose and recovered in small noisy-image datasets and several EEG patients.
FGSM-trained CNNs recovered robust test accuracy after an intermediate decline.
Large adversarially trained models showed renewed test-error improvement after robust overfitting.
With weak regularization, the second test-error descent occurred exponentially later as noise increased.
Weakly regularized ResNet18 and teacher-student models exhibited fall-rise-fall test error.
Wide ResNet18 models showed epoch-wise double descent with standard one-hot training.
All six noisy-label VGG and ResNet settings showed epoch-wise double descent in classification error.
ERM-trained ResNet-18 reproduced epoch-wise double descent with noisy labels.
Wide ResNet18 models showed pronounced epoch-wise double descent above the label-noise threshold.
WideResNet16 models exhibited epoch-wise double descent on noisy CIFAR10.
ConvNets and ResNet18s showed epoch-wise double descent beyond the interpolation threshold.
Regression theory with direction-dependent variation yielded multiple test-error descents over training time.
Noisy-label networks showed epoch-wise double descent on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100.
Transfer learning with sufficiently large target datasets produced test-error peaks near interpolation.
An 800M transformer showed fall-rise-fall test loss with heavily repeated training data.
A CNN without weight decay showed epoch-wise double descent on noisy CIFAR-10.
The four-layer GRU showed epoch-wise double descent in validation token accuracy.
Larger OPT models showed rising and recovering perplexity on selected held-out tokens.
The underwater acoustic baseline showed double descent in test loss during training.
Autoformer and Informer validation losses recovered below their first minima after intermediate deterioration.
A modular-arithmetic transformer's validation loss fell, rose, and dropped to zero at grokking.
Large ConvNets and ResNet18s showed epoch-wise double descent during accelerated interpolation.
GPT-2 test loss rose around 200 training epochs before falling across longer runs.
Noisy-label training produced fall-rise-fall test error on CIFAR100 and TinyImagenet.
Transformers learning modular division showed fall-rise-fall test loss over training.
ResNet18, DenseNet121, and BERT exhibited epoch-wise double descent on noisy datasets.
Linear and diffusion models showed repeated descents in out-of-distribution loss over training.
Decoupled linear networks showed fall-rise-fall generalization error in some parameter ranges.
Noisy nonlinear autoencoders exhibited epoch-wise double descent across noise and signal-to-noise levels.
Linear theory permitted double descent when noise was learned before slower signal components.
Transformers on algorithmic tasks showed a training-time hump followed by a second descent.
Particle-physics transformers and MLPs showed fall-rise-fall test error over epochs.
Fine-tuned PEGASUS validation scores recovered beyond early peaks after producing gibberish.
ResNet18 test accuracy showed double ascent under symmetric label noise.
Yelp LSTMs showed repeated test-loss rises and drops across all tested seeds.
ResNet18 showed epoch-wise double descent with both pretrained and scratch initialization.
The UNet-10 diffusion student showed fall-rise-fall generalization error during distillation.
Noisy-label ResNet-18 generalized best well after the early-stopping epoch.
MLP7 test loss declined again after prolonged noisy-label fitting.
Large U-Nets showed fall-rise-fall test loss, with sharper second descents at larger widths.
Overparameterized CIFAR-10 models showed epoch-wise double descent under both IL and ML.
Dynamical-system transformers showed temporal double descent on familiar and unseen systems.
ResNet18 test accuracy followed a fall-rise-fall trajectory at both tested noise levels.
Shallow linear students lacked a second test-error descent over training.
Random-feature test loss rose after initial improvement without recovering over the observed training period.
Rescaled step sizes or initialization eliminated or reduced epoch-wise double descent.
Most adversarial training trajectories lacked a second descent within 200–500 epochs.
Self-adaptive training substantially reduced the epoch-wise test-error peak.
ImageNet subset error largely plateaued, with only slight deterioration reduced by larger models.
Random-feature test error fell, plateaued, and rose without a second descent.
Natural gradient made bias monotonic; gradient descent did too with a direction-independent signal prior.
More data, clean labels, and intermediate learning rates removed the observed double-descent pattern.
Adversarially trained ResNet-18 error lacked a second descent, with SiLU showing little deterioration.
GradAlign prevented the intermediate robustness decline during FGSM training.
Smaller adversarial models lacked full double descent, and learning-rate schedules affected recovery.
Strong overparameterization yielded monotonic descent with two plateaus rather than an intermediate error rise.
Intermediate regularization or very slowly learned features prevented a second test-error descent.
Input concatenation reduced epoch-wise double descent and removed it on CIFAR-100.
Small noisy-label MNIST networks plateaued at high error after overfitting without a second descent.
Epoch-wise double descent disappeared without label noise and weakened under alternative loss metrics.
Self-adaptive training left only a slight bump before monotonic improvement.
Clean-label WR28-8 test error fell throughout both training phases without an intermediate rise.
Low noise, narrow networks, or output layers trained to convergence suppressed epoch-wise double descent.
Clean-label test error decreased and plateaued across tested widths without double descent.
Noisy regression MLPs overfit after approaching Bayes error without a second descent.
ResNet18 showed no clean-data error rise or noisy-data second descent within 200 epochs.
Freezing, larger source datasets, and small targets reduced or eliminated transfer-learning double descent.
DeepONet error fell then rose without a second descent during training.
The transformer showed a long loss plateau with 50% repeated data.
An overparameterized ReLU network showed no temporal double descent on noisy synthetic data.
Smaller GRUs lacked double descent, while automatic text metrics showed it weakly.
Large depth-eight networks showed only hints of epoch-wise double descent.
Aggregate OPT perplexity declined monotonically, while selected-token recovery depended on model size.
Informer on Traffic kept overfitting through 1,000 epochs without a second descent.
Grokking validation accuracy plateaued before improving, without the intermediate deterioration seen in loss.
Near-threshold networks lacked a second descent, while smaller networks plateaued.
Test accuracy never decreased during training without label noise.
Mixup over-training produced falling then rising test error without a second descent.
Epoch-wise double descent was faint in accuracy and more pronounced in loss.
Polynomial regression showed worsening then improving generalization only at a particular parameter setting.
Clean CIFAR-10-N, Income, and Reddit-12k lacked epoch-wise double descent.
High-dimensional SIM and one-layer linear models showed monotonic learning dynamics.
Epoch-wise double descent required particular differences in how spectral components or layers changed during training.
Large MLPs showed no epoch-wise double descent on balanced particle physics data.
Diffusion models’ held-out loss rose at memorization onset without a subsequent descent.
PEGASUS scores either degraded without recovery or improved nearly monotonically, depending on checkpoint.
ResNet18 test accuracy increased throughout training without label noise.
Separate annealed runs showed validation loss falling then rising with increased data repetition.
ResNet18 lacked double descent without label noise; its noisy second descent never beat early stopping.
Diffusion distillation lacked a second descent when little data was available.
Repeated-data language models showed falling then rising loss without recovery by epoch 32.
Multistep scheduling made early stopping coincide with best accuracy.
Smaller MLPs plateaued or worsened without a second descent.
Smaller U-Nets showed monotonic improvement or overfitting without a second descent.
Quantum-network test error plateaued before reaching zero, without a reported intermediate rise.
Quadratic-network MSE fell then rose without a reported second descent.
Auto MPG error ended above its early minimum; how it changed in between remained unclear.
Under high noise, models learning tones overfit without recovery; low-noise accuracy declined only slightly.
Narrow mutual-learning networks improved monotonically or overfit without a second descent.
Clean-label ResNet18 accuracy rose monotonically without epoch-wise double descent.
An underparameterized model reached a late accuracy plateau without a grokking upswing.
Boosting test risk followed a U-shaped trajectory without a reported second descent.
Small or shallow CNNs overfit random labels without recovering within the training window.
ResNet50 ImageNet test loss worsened after its mid-training minimum without recovering.
Tabular MLP sweeps found no strong evidence of epoch-wise double descent.
Recurrent-network test losses rose smoothly after early minima without a second descent.
Larger image classifiers reached their best error without an intervening rise.

wording_issues.issue: Classification error, CE/MSE, distributional PFD and validation summarization scores are different outcomes. Zero-one double descent can be weak in CE/MSE, while LSTM loss cycles do not carry over to classification accuracy. The summarization study defers test evaluation.

GPT-2 and Llama-style epoch sweeps compare separately trained endpoints. The Llama-style runs each anneal their learning-rate schedule to zero; their endpoint improvement followed by overfitting leaves the within-run V2 trajectory cannot_determine, with no V2 verdict. OPT uses selected checkpoints and training FLOPs. Its selected-token rise and recovery are partial for strict V2 because the textual description does not separately establish an initial decrease; this warrants limits_scope rather than supports.
The unqualified wording omits conditions where the curve is absent or incomplete: low noise, smaller capacity, deliberate tabular-network sweeps and smaller diffusion widths.
Some results have repeated or multiple temporal descents rather than a single sequence. The compositional multiple-descent demonstrations use selected signal strengths and tuned initialization seeds.

Rise-then-fall descriptions alone do not establish an initial decrease. The polynomial-grokking example requires this distinction; selected OPT-token rise and recovery are partial for strict V2 and warrant limits_scope rather than supports. A fall-plateau-fall QNN trajectory lacks the required rise. The structured-feature example establishes a late accuracy plateau and no late grokking transition, but does not establish the complete earlier error trajectory: its V2 state is cannot_determine, with no V2 verdict.

The late fall need not beat the first minimum. ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 in arXiv:2503.02302 exhibits the required trajectory even though the second descent does not reach a lower error than the first; this supports V2. Another ResNet study reports noise-dependent cases where later training is better; forecasting reports both possibilities. Coincident early-stopping and best-accuracy epochs under the multistep schedule in 10.1007/s00521-026-12575-1 do not exclude a later shallower descent: the V2 state remains cannot_determine, with no V2 verdict.

Validation loss, teacher-forced token accuracy and outcomes measured with corrupted validation labels need their evaluation conditions stated. They do not directly establish the same curve in clean test classification error.

Selected-token perplexity can rise and recover while aggregate validation perplexity decreases monotonically. The selected-subset description does not separately establish an initial decrease, so it is partial for strict V2 and warrants limits_scope rather than supports. It also does not establish aggregate epoch-wise double descent.

A minimum and a higher endpoint, or a scalar final-minus-minimum gap, cannot establish the complete trajectory. Auto MPG's early minimum and higher final risk do not distinguish a subsequent monotonic rise from an intervening peak and recovery: its V2 state is cannot_determine, with no V2 verdict. The missing trajectory is untested rather than a demonstrated scope limitation. Scalar repeated-data language-model gaps are also marked cannot_determine.

method_sensitivity.what: The ResNet18 noise threshold is setup-specific. A binary CIFAR experiment requires noise in both training and validation labels; noisy training with clean validation lacks the effect. In arXiv:2503.02302, CIFAR-10 ResNet18 lacks double descent with clean labels and exhibits it with noisy labels; the reported fall-rise-fall supports V2 even when the second minimum remains above the first. In arXiv:2507.08686, clean CIFAR-100 lacks double ascent in test accuracy, whereas 20% symmetric training-label noise shows it with clean test labels. That figure's architecture is unspecified, and the clean/noisy training recipes also differ.

CNN width changes monotone improvement into ordinary overfitting and then full double descent. MLP depth changes recovery even when smaller models train longer. For GRUs with hidden size 3072, validation token accuracy shows the effect in the 4-layer model, while the 1- and 2-layer models are described as too small to exhibit it. The separately reported cross-entropy effect has no specified model configuration. Diffusion U-Nets likewise change from monotone improvement through fall-rise to fall-rise-fall with increasing width.

method_sensitivity.factor: Layer learning rates, initialization and readout optimization
method_sensitivity.what: Feature/layer-specific step sizes and initialization scales change or remove the curve. Analytically converging the final readout removes it in a ResNet18 intervention. Switching GD to NGD makes the stated linear-regression bias trajectory monotone.

method_sensitivity.factor: Regularization, targets, input construction and transfer
method_sensitivity.what: In CIFAR-10 ResNet18, small weight decay permits epoch-wise double descent, whereas intermediate weight decay removes the second descent and leaves conventional overfitting. This observes regularization-dependent removal; disappearance under optimally tuned regularization is untested. Self-adaptive targets diminish the peak. Concatenating inputs changes or removes the curve. Transfer outcomes vary with target size, source size, frozen layers and architecture.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning-rate schedule, sampling cadence and observation window
method_sensitivity.what: The checkpoint study reports time-wise double descent under linear and restarted-cosine schedules. Under multistep scheduling, early stopping and best accuracy coincide; the complete V2 shape remains undetermined because a later shallower descent is not excluded. In adversarial training, constant, cyclic and cosine schedules show recovery, whereas piecewise decay shows robust overfitting without observed recovery: partial V2, with the authors suggesting a second descent might be delayed by the extremely small late learning rate. The aliasing study reports learning-rate and validation-sampling sensitivity. The noisy CIFAR-100 accuracy result uses warm restarts without isolating their causal contribution.

method_sensitivity.factor: Outcome metric, descriptor and post-hoc evaluation
method_sensitivity.what: Zero-one error versus CE/MSE changes visibility. Temperature scaling removes a reported base-loss double descent in the post-hoc study; its classification-error curves remain separate evidence. Changing SSCD to DINOv2 flattens the diffusion-distillation rise. LSTM loss cycles are not mirrored by classification accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Repeated data, token selection and replacement
method_sensitivity.what: Changing repeated fraction from 90% to 50% turns the 800M transformer's bump into a plateau. OPT curves depend on token-selection model and training point. Tokens selected after 10% of OPT 1.3B training show rise and recovery in OPT 6.7B, 13B, 30B and 175B, but an initial decrease is not separately established: partial V2. For OPT-175B-selected tokens, r22 reports a late rise without recovery, also partial; §3.2 gives selection at 20% of training, while Figure 4's caption gives 10%. GPT-2 sweeps use separate endpoints. Korean-text token replacement shifts the loss minimum while both conditions still lack recovery within 32 epochs.

Linear temporal shapes depend on covariance eigenvalues, singular values and layer dynamics. Random-feature models switch between plateaus and a bump under different ratios/noise settings. Non-isotropic regression produces multiple descents. In compositional OOD regression, a 4-layer linear MLP shows fall-rise-fall loss at d = 2 but lacks non-monotonic loss at d = 64; depth also affects the outcome. Separate multiple-descent demonstrations use tuned seeds and selected signal strengths.

Particle MLPs show the curve on unbalanced larger data but not balanced smaller data, leaving balance and size confounded. PEGASUS recovery changes with subset size and checkpoint: larger subsets recover for pegasus-large/xsum, while pegasus-x-base improves nearly monotonically.

The Yelp LSTM changes from zero reported loss descents to repeated descents when learning rate and hidden size change together, preventing attribution to either alone; IMDb SGD experiments lack multiple descents. In the dynamical-system transformer, longer context strengthens the curve and unseen-system loss has a separate earlier descent.
